The uncovered failure mode is: a forbidden routing state is silently admitted because the refusal guard is dead.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a downstream guard catches the same mismatched lease before it can propagate, the refusal guard's death is less severe and may drop in priority.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the firewall is not deployed in any production configuration (i.e., it is test-only scaffolding), the blast radius is smaller than assumed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If SCHOOL_ROUTE_LEASE_MISMATCH and SCHOOL_ROUTE_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH require different test fixtures, two tests are needed, slightly raising the cost.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"PARKED.md states that disabling the firewall's lease-mismatch refusal leaves the entire suite green and no test asserts either SCHOOL_ROUTE_LEASE_MISMATCH or SCHOOL_ROUTE_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH. The cheapest test is a single unit test that constructs a request with a mismatched lease and asserts the specific error code is raised. This directly catches the guard's death by failing if the refusal is disabled. It is second in priority because the failure mode is a security policy silent failure: a routing state that should be refused is admitted, but the append-only record itself is not corrupted. This is lower blast radius than digest corruption but higher than routing rot or recovery-path failure because it silently violates an active firewall policy.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
